conventions.convention: Spacetime is four-dimensional Minkowski space with signature (−,+,+,+), x⁰=ct, and natural units c=ℏ=1.
Right-principal-bundle conventions give F_A=dA+½[A∧A] and D_μψ=∂_μψ+ρ_*(A_μ)ψ.

The finite operator quotient identifies exactly the explicitly declared invariant relations. Algebraic invariance must either be verified to match physical invariance or be labelled a formal algebraic selection.

An operator of weight Δ enters as ζ^ℓ C(μ_W)O/Λ_op^(Δ−4), with dimensionless C and ζ and positive invariant Λ_op of weight one. Operator, regulator, threshold, external-energy and Wilsonian scales remain distinct.
H and its independent dual are commuting scalar variables; the real-action slice imposes H̃=H†. The example uses r=0, q=6, D_max=6, loop order zero and zero relation space.

The scalar EOM example uses compactly supported real fields and variations, E₀=(□−m²)φ, and formal first-order bookkeeping in Λ_op⁻². Its remainder denotes higher formal order, without a numerical error estimate or quantum equivalence claim.

load_bearing.statement: A physical EFT operator contract records selected field, symmetry, finite-jet, field-degree, relation, coefficient and truncation data. Its selected quotient is Q_D=V_D/(R̃_D∩V_D), identifying exactly the declared relations. The quotient alone establishes no action, off-shell Green-function, quantum-measure or scattering equivalence.

In the declared quotient, φ²∂_μφ∂^μφ represents −m²φ⁴/3. The substitution φ_old=φ+Cφ³/(3Λ_op²) changes S₀+S₆ to S₀−Cm²∫φ⁴/(3Λ_op²)+O(Λ_op⁻⁴), as an action-level statement at the retained formal order only.

For the stated scalar SU(2) model, O₂=H̃H, O₄=(H̃H)² and O₆=(H̃H)³ are gauge-invariant scalar polynomials of engineering dimensions 2, 4 and 6; C₆O₆/Λ_op² has dimension four, and ε_ab HᵃHᵇ vanishes for commuting components.

published_dependencies.used_for: The precise inherited AC_ω assumption: every countable family of nonempty sets admits a choice function. No arbitrary-index choice is inferred.
The model-data supplier's natural-unit and engineering-dimension convention, including the distinction between canonical engineering dimensions and interacting scaling dimensions.
The local-operator supplier's complex reductive-group hypothesis and its fixed-vector definition of unipotence.

concerns.concern: The dimension-six quotient needs an explicit graded treatment of the mass spurion. The Example specifies the finite-jet module as the complexification of the scalar field and fixes m≥0 as a parameter, then declares φ³(□−m²)φ a homogeneous dimension-six relation. In the cited def-aqft-local-operator-and-dimension, however, P_{r,q,D} is a complex vector space graded by field-jet generator weights. For a fixed nonzero numerical m, m²φ⁴ is a complex scalar multiple of a weight-four monomial, whereas φ³□φ has weight six. Consequently their difference is not in the supplied W₆, and the claimed quotient class of −m²φ⁴/3 is unsupported as currently defined. Assigning a physical engineering dimension to a fixed coefficient does not itself extend that polynomial grading. Specify formal spurion generators or a graded coefficient construction, including how specialization and the degree cutoff work. The action substitution, its signs, and its explicit higher-order polynomial terms check independently.

The Definition requires a finite-dimensional action of SO⁺(1,3) on all spacetime indices but supplies no spin-cover alternative. This leaves the advertised fermionic interface inadequate for the Weyl fields used by post-aqft-smeft-model and the supersymmetric consumer. A Weyl representation is a representation of Spin⁺(1,3)≅SL(2,C); a 2π rotation acts as −I, so it does not descend to SO⁺(1,3). Clarify the permitted covering group, its projection to the coordinate Lorentz group, and its field/jet action, then check the downstream instances. This distinction is explicit in David Tong's QFT notes §4.4, equations (4.365)–(4.368): https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/qft/qfthtml/S4.html.
